title: World-space canvas (canvas@1)
summary: A world-space canvas in the native overlay host: primitives, anchors, caps and a per-tick camera snapshot, with the radar view, so producers draw in game with no per-layer game-side code.

demand.note: Bridge proposal A as agreed: the bridge draws, Holotable decides what. Schema to Holotable for review before building.

title: Canvas keys and canvas.visible
summary: Show, hide and mode keys for the canvas through the bridge's own key route, rebindable in CET, with a canvas.visible state.

demand.note: Show and hide while playing, without opening CET (CET blocks input).

title: Read-only Lua snapshot for CET modules
summary: A read-only snapshot for Holotable's CET module: V, XF actors, incidents, supervisor holds and recorder gaps, refreshed a few times a second.

demand.note: Lets the overlay work with no other XF program running (bridge proposal B).

title: The display access class and canvas.feed
summary: A display access class and a canvas.feed command usable from read-only connections, so producers such as the Story Engine can draw in game in bounded batches (1-4 Hz).

demand.note: Bridge proposal C. Story Engine layers reach the overlay through it.

title: Published probe and scene results (observe.result)
summary: A bounded observe.result session event with the command, the caller's cid and the result whenever a writer calls world_probe, scene_read or world_district, adding no game-thread work.

demand.note: Lets Holotable draw what sessions already asked, at no extra game cost.

title: The XfCanvasPlate token
summary: A canvas plate style token (the translucent backing behind overlay panels and labels, about 72 % opacity) themed with XF Studio's tokens in dark and light.

demand.note: The design comes from the UI component track; the bridge exposes the token to canvas@1.

title: Read-only recorder status
summary: A read-only command answered on the bridge thread (no game-thread call, no lease, no ack) that reports whether the recorder is active and its current run: { active, run, session, world, channels, start, latest, stopReason }, so an observer can find the run to read with game.catchup.

demand.note: Holotable's Live game row polls it every 5 s, only while the view is shown. Today InfoJson() and Status() expose no recorder state, and game.catchup needs a positive run.
